validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. A Gazprom release of 21 November 2008 says it was commissioned in stages, Barnaul to Biysk in November 2006, the Belokurikha branch in October 2007 and Biysk to Gorno-Altaysk in November 2008, about 320 km in all.

verifications.note: пропускная способность газопровода Барнаул – Бийск – Горно-Алтайск всего 1,7 млрд

fills.researcher_notes: An Altapress article says the throughput of the Barnaul, Biysk and Gorno-Altaysk gas pipeline is only 1.7 billion cubic meters, and the context is a yearly volume. That matches the sheet value of 1.7 bcm/y. It is one article, and it gives the figure in passing while comparing it with a planned export line.

fills.researcher_notes: Both pages support only part of the sheet value. Altapress says the pipes of the existing line are 300 to 700 mm. Continent Siberia of May 2007 says the Ob river crossing has a main pipe of 520 mm and a spare 300 mm pipe. Neither page lists 325 or 720 mm. The sheet value is kept at low confidence.

Continent Siberia of May 2007 says Tomsktransgaz, a Gazprom subsidiary, was the customer for the line and that its Altai linear production department organized the construction. That is the company now called Gazprom Transgaz Tomsk. The page is from 2007 and says who built the line, not who runs it today, so the tier is low.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Gazprom says the line was commissioned in November 2008. Altapress reports the line in use, with 37 percent of its capacity used in 2013.
